title: need good book recommendations for aspiring film critics

commenti.body:
The Age of Movies: Selected Writings of Pauline Kael.

I only just started reading it yesterday, but it's pretty good. Lots of different sections deal with different movies, aspects of filmmaking, and film cristism. And since it is a collection of selected writing, you can read the chapters in any order.

Adventures in the Dcreen Trade: A Personal view of Hollywood is a wonderful book by screenwriter William Goldman.

I honestly think you should steer away from books about movies. Read books that entice your critical thinking, not just something to learn more about cinema. When you watch a movie and it comes time to write about it, learn it then. Watch a YouTube video, or read something about it. You don't need to learn NOW why Bicycle Thieves is bla bla bla, you can do it later. 

Read books with high moral debates because those happen in movies. Read books about creative people, writers, or movie makers, so you can connect with the director. Read character studies or psychology books, so you understand the character.

He’s a relatively dry read if you’re going from cover to cover, but there is no better critic for developing an understanding of film form than David Bordwell. Reading Film Art, The Classical Hollywood Cinema, or The Way Hollywood Tells It will greatly expand anyone’s understanding of how film works on a formal level.

Believe it or not, film criticism has its own type of structure and cadence that you should get familiar with. Learning about the actual craft will add to your knowledge of course, but in my opinion, it's not as important as simply reading other influential critics and getting a feel for the thing. In college, I walked into the student newspaper and asked if I could write for them (I was a journalism major at the time). They asked me if I could write film reviews, since the previous one quit, and I lied and said I could. To learn, I simply sat down and read a countless amount of Roger Ebert reviews, since he was supposedly one of the best writers at the time and got right to it, with nobody questioning my ability or background afterwards. Above all, people are going to (rightfully) judge your work by the quality of your insight and writing ability.

I like Mark Cousins personally.

One of the few who acknowledges the plurality of canons and the high and low.

There's only so much that can be learned from the typical and there are huge blind spots.

Not a book per se, but you can find all editions of Cahiers du Cinema translated in english to download online.

Andre Bazin is always the safest choice when it comes to the French New Wave. American Criticism is very vast and always conflicting. I prefer Andrew Sarris, for example, instead of Kael or Ebert. It depends on wich approach you like it better. 

An introductory book that covers almost all aspects of cinema is How To Watch a Movie by David Thomson. A good beginnig  that i would recommend.
